newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - April 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - April 8.

text.p: Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In results which indicate the Federal Government's Budget pledge to boost jobs growth by 1.5 per cent is under threat, the Australian Chamber of Manufacturing released a study yesterday showing the industry's level of output has been virtually static this financial year, and new job figures from the ANZ Banking Group reveal the job vacancy series only rose by 0.4 per cent in trend terms in March. Page 1.

Defence Minister Ian McLachlan will release the final report of the Federal Government's Defence Efficiency Review, a wide-ranging review of the Defence Department which has alarmed many of the Department's 112,000 uniformed and civilian employees who fear for their jobs. The report is expected to recommend savings of more than A$1 billion in Australia's annual A$10 billion annual defence budget. Page 3.

Australian Democrats Leader Cheryl Kernot yesterday increased the pressure on controversial Independent Senator Mal Colston after receiving advice from high-ranking Senate Department officials that Colston may not be a fit and proper person to be Senate Deputy President. Page 3.

Victorian Treasurer Alan Stockdale revealed yesterday the State Government would contest legal action launched by one of Australia's largest stevedoring companies, Patrick Stevedoring, against the Melbourne Port Corporation's move to invite Hong Kong Shiping giant Orient Overseas Container Line to operate a container-handling terminal in the port. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Federal Government sources told The Australian yesterday the Treasury is preparing plans recommending the one per cent Medicare levy surcharge on high income earners without private health insurance, due to come into effect on July 1, be significantly increased in the upcoming Budget. Page 1.

Yesterday saw the start of what is being hailed as a landmark case to rival the famous 1925 Scopes monkey trial in America - the case against Christian scientist Allen Roberts and the Ark Search Association Associated concerning the alleged finding of Noa's Ark. University of Melbourne earth sciences senior lecturer Ian Plimer is using Australia's trade practices and fair trading laws to contest Roberts' claim that he found Noah's Ark near Mount Ararat in eastern Turkey. Page 1.

According to new research by the Insurance and Superannuation Commission, people who earn less than A$400-a-week put aside more of their salary for superannuation that higher income earners, indicating super is becoming more popular with low-income earners. The findings covered workers aged 45 or over who choose to contribute their own money to superannuation. Page 1.

In a move which, although a good indication of an improvement in Australia's relations with China, presents a fresh challenge for the Howard Government in dealing with controversial issues such as human rights, China has broken a ban on ministerial travel to Australia, with upcoming visits by two high-ranking Chinese ministers planned within the next three years. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The New South Wales Government has ordered State Rail to slash A$200 million from its budget in what is the biggest cut to a government department thus far. The Labor Government is facing a A$1 billion shortfall in this year's budget, and the cut to State Rail will slice 15 per cent in real terms from the rail budget of A$1.4 billion. Page 1.

A violent protest was held at Sydney University last night after the university senate agreed on a proposal which could mean the cost of some degrees rising to around A$100,000. Angry students smashed windows and others occupied part of the main building as one student was taken away by security gaurds after jumping through a window, showering officials with broken glass. Page 1.

Following passionate debate in Federal Cabinet last night, the Government has agreed to ban degrading, debasing and demeaning scenes in X-rated material. However, it agreed non-violent sex will still be legal and also decided to replace the X-rated categry with a non-violent erotica category (NVE) which will be more strictly defined. Page 1.

A study by the Broken Hill Environmental Lead Centre has found blood-lead levels in Broken Hill children remain dangerously high, three years after a A$13 million Health Department program began to combat the problem. Page 3.
THE AGE

In a surprise ruling which appeared to be a rebuff for conservative forces within Federal Cabinet, the Cabinet last night effectively endorsed the continued sale of pornographic videos and gave the green light for the Galaxy pay-TV channel to continue its late night screenings of the Nightmoves program, providing its access is limited by a PIN code. Page 1.

Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett yesterday described as "very regrettable" a move by the Carlton Australian Football League Club to take the Greg Williams case to the Supreme Court. Carlton seeks to have Williams' nine-match suspension for pushing an umpire overturned, a move Kennett says will "probably do sport generally a great deal of harm". Page 1.

New Australian Bureau of Statistics data has revealed Australia's last recession has left a significant residue of unemployment and underemployment. The detailed figures show almost 600,000 families - one in eight - have one or more members unemployed. Seventy five per cent of the 600,000 are traditional families headed by couples. Page 1.

Australian Unity, Victoria's third-largest private health fund insuring almost 250,000 Victorians, has informed the Federal Government it plans to follow its competitors and raise premiums for most of its health insurance tables by an average 11 per cent from May 1. Page 1.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
